inspectedText: Bredius accepted Emmaus in1937 and other experts endorsed it. Van Meegeren claimed authorship after accusation over the Adulteress sale to Göring’s agent. Some continued defending authenticity. Workshop evidence and tests supported modern authorship. Later claims of having detected the fraud early are not uniformly documented; named exceptions had period records. Decoen later disputed the technical conclusions.
quality: Footnoted specialist research separating period criticism, material evidence, later claims and disputed retrospection.
limitations: Secondary legal description uses treason broadly; narration instead says suspicion of collaboration.
Painting during the trial denotes the extended1945–47 proceedings, not proven painting in1947courtroom.
Some experts rejected the work; never claim unanimous acceptance.
